body.prompt:
Use case: ChandRush Chapter 02 location reference plate L03_C, a medium three-quarter view of the empty round two-tray loading table in Food Street, establishing its mechanism before any packs are loaded.
Asset: one 4:3 landscape scenic image of an empty location, no characters.
Input images:
- Image 1: the approved Food Street master, seen from Lantern Street. Use it for: the round indigo-and-brass loading table on its fixed pedestal with the brass two-tray cradle, the cream packing bench and Return Walk doorway on the near-left, the brass sixteen-cup trolley, pale wet-sheen paving, indigo timber, brass lamps and the moonlit look. Ignore: all white label boxes, annotation words and arrows; the wooden cart, the brass bowls and the spills on the floor (not in this view).
Camera and framing: medium three-quarter view from the Lantern Street (entrance) side of the central loading table, at standing eye height, slightly above table level, looking towards the closed Parade end. The table sits centre to centre-right. The entrance-side tray is nearest the camera; the far tray points away towards the closed Parade end in the background. Along the left edge of the frame, nearer the camera than the table, are the pale packing-bench edge and the Return Walk doorway. The whole pedestal, the brake housing and the paving all round the table are visible.
Place and construction: the round indigo timber table top has a brass edge band and stands on a fixed pedestal. A rotating brass head in its centre carries a centrally pivoted cradle. Two matching shallow rectangular brass trays sit at equal distances on opposite sides of the pivot, one towards the camera (Lantern Street) and one towards the Parade end. The trays are identical in size and shape. Small mechanical stop blocks under the cradle limit tilt to a shallow angle. On the table's left side, the packing-bench side, is a brass brake housing with two separate controls: a rotation latch (a small brass bolt) and a separate squeeze lever for the tilt damper. The brass delivery trolley from Image 1 is parked at screen-left beside the packing bench, clear of the trays' sweep: an upper carrier with sixteen cup sockets and a separate lower snack shelf.
State at this moment (exact):
1. Both brass trays are completely empty: bare brass, no packs, no objects.
2. Tilt: the near (entrance-side) tray rests slightly lower, on its shallow mechanical stop; the far tray is slightly higher. The tilt is small but visible.
3. Rotation latch: engaged, the brass bolt pushed into its notch.
4. Tilt-damper squeeze lever: released, sitting up away from the housing in its rest position.
5. Trolley: exactly 16 (sixteen) empty brass cups standing in its upper carrier in 4 (four) rows of 4 (four); the lower snack tray is empty. All four trolley wheels touch the paving.
6. The table pedestal stands firmly on the paving.
7. The Return Walk threshold is clear. A clear ring of paving runs all round the table outside the trays' reach, and the near-side paving in front of the camera is clear.
Physical inscriptions: none. No numbers, letters or words anywhere: no tray tags, no signs.
Keep clear and visible: paving beside the brake housing on the packing-bench side; the latch and the squeeze lever; the clear route around the tray edges; the near-side paving in the foreground; the tilted tray edges and the central pivot.
Light: fixed amber lamps lit, cool full-moon light; brass highlights on the trays.
Do not show: any pack on a tray or the floor; level trays; the damper lever pressed down; cups other than 16; filled cups; the cart, bowls or spills; any person, hand or animal; label boxes or arrows from Image 1.

Look and finish (same for every ChandRush location plate): premium semi-realistic painterly 2.5D graphic-novel illustration that matches the supplied ChandRush masters, a blend of illustration and reality. It is painterly in finish but crisp and precise in drawing. Materials and light have near-photographic conviction while forms stay clean, idealised and orderly, like a high-end storybook. ChandRush is an ancient travelling fair with grand, mystic, magical scale and real architectural detailing: dimensional deep-indigo and ultramarine painted timber with visible grain, joinery, rivets and edge banding; warm polished and cast brass with bright specular edges and a light patina; pale cream stone worktops and pale irregular stone paving with a light wet sheen and crisp reflections; layered fabric canopies; restrained circular celestial ornament (full-moon discs, rings, small eight-point stars) in gold and brass. Palette: ultramarine, cobalt, indigo and navy against amber, honey-gold and brass, with strong warm-cool contrast, saturated but natural, never neon. Light: fixed amber task lamps cast clean, well-defined warm pools, their glow held tight around the lamp glass with no spreading halo; cool full-moon light edges roofs, canopy gaps, stone and brass; deep, rich shadows that keep readable detail. Clarity: clear, dry night air with no haze, fog, mist, smoke or airborne dust. Crisp edges and high micro-contrast. Sharp, clean textures in wood grain, brass and stone, as in a high-resolution photograph. True deep darks and clean colours, never a milky, washed-out or glowing veil over the image, never soft focus. The background stays crisp and only slightly darker with distance. Ornament is dense above eye level and on frames; floors, worktops and mechanisms stay open, clean and readable.

Production rules (apply to every plate):
- Frame: one 4:3 landscape scenic image filling the whole canvas edge to edge. No border, title band, panel frame, vignette box or blank margin.
- Lettering: the only lettering allowed is the physical inscriptions listed above, rendered exactly as written, letter for letter, with each minus sign as a true minus sign. No other words, numbers or symbols anywhere. No title, caption, callout, label box, leader line, arrow, legend, watermark or signature: titles and callouts are added later by the production team.
- Reference images: their titles, annotation words, label boxes and arrows only identify places for you. Reproduce none of them.
- Empty location: no people, children, helpers, wooden figures, animals, hands, shadows of figures or silhouettes. The place waits, ready for characters to be added later.
- Counts and states are exact as stated. Add no extra copies of any counted object and no extra devices, cards, lamps or tiles.
- Unlit means unlit: clear or smoky glass with no flame, no inner glow and no bloom. Lit lamps glow only at their own glass.
- Avoid: haze, fog, mist, bloom halos, soft focus, a low-contrast or milky wash, modern signage, plastic, neon, sci-fi screens, crowds, text on fabric or banners, mirrored or garbled lettering, duplicated objects, warped or melted geometry, a second moon in the sky, a crescent moon.

Use case: same-camera state change of Image 1 for ChandRush plate L03_E, the loading table with balanced loads. It is used in a counting scene, so the pack counts must be exactly right and easy to count.
Asset: one 4:3 landscape scenic image, identical camera to Image 1.
Input images:
- Image 1: the approved plate L03_D. Keep its camera, framing, perspective, table, cradle, pivot, brake housing, bench strip, paving, materials, colours, lighting, pack design and tag style exactly. The two trays keep exactly the same size, shape and position as in Image 1.
- Image 2: the approved Food Street master. Use it only for finish and materials. Ignore: its label boxes, annotation words, arrows, cart, bowls and trolley.
Change only:
1. Near (entrance-side) tray, lower half of frame: exactly 20 (twenty) packs, laid flat in a grid of 4 (four) rows of 5 (five), single layer, small even gaps, centred with a band of bare brass tray surface left around the grid.
2. Far (Parade-side) tray, upper half of frame: exactly 20 (twenty) packs, laid flat in a grid of 4 (four) rows of 5 (five), the same layout, with bare brass margin around it.
3. Total exactly 40 (forty) packs, all on the two trays. Same identical pack design as Image 1. No stacking, no packs off the trays.
4. Tilt: both trays are now level with each other, at equal height; the cradle arm is horizontal.
5. Tray tags: the near tray's tag reads "20"; the far tray's tag reads "20".
Everything else stays exactly as in Image 1, including the tray size (each still big enough for a 5 by 5 grid), the rotation latch engaged in its notch, the tilt-damper squeeze lever pressed down, the bench strip at lower-left and the clear pivot.
Physical inscriptions after the change (render exactly, nothing else): brass tag on the near tray's outer rim reading "20"; brass tag on the far tray's outer rim reading "20"; each about one fifteenth of the frame width, bold legible numerals. No other numbers, letters or words.
Keep clear and visible: the depressed squeeze lever; both trays' outer rims; both tags; the pivot; bare margins around each grid.
Do not show: 19 or 21 packs on either tray; a 5×5 grid; tags "25" or "15"; tilted trays; smaller trays; any person, hand or animal.

Use case: ChandRush Chapter 02 location reference plate L05_B, a low three-quarter view of the Food Street drink counter from its entrance end, at the eye height of a small child. Both recipe jug levels must sit exactly at the same mark.
Asset: one 4:3 landscape scenic image of an empty location, no characters.
Input images:
- Image 1: the approved plate L05_A, the drink counter seen straight on. Use it for: the exact design of the two teal glazed recipe jugs (body, handle, base, narrow clear sight window with brass tick scale on the front), the broad brass urn with its front tap, the cream stone slab, indigo panelled timber with brass corner fittings and star-medallion panels, the brass work lamp above-left, the paving. Ignore: the recipe card and its lettering; the reserve bottle and transfer jug (not needed).
- Image 2: the approved Food Street master. Use it only for finish and light. Ignore: all label boxes, annotation words and arrows; the cart, bowls, trolley and table.
Camera and framing: low medium three-quarter view from the entrance end of the drink counter, camera below the counter top (about knee to waist height), looking along and up at the counter's aisle-facing front. The counter runs from near frame-right into the distance at frame-left (towards the Parade end). Visible: paving in the bottom third, the indigo timber support and panels, the cream stone front lip, and above it the front-facing sides of the two teal recipe jugs, standing together left of centre, with handles and sight windows turned towards the aisle and camera. Part of the brass urn and its closed tap at the right, nearer the camera. The work-lamp bracket visible high on the backdrop. Jug tops may be cut off or hidden by the slab angle.
State at this moment (exact):
1. Left recipe jug: pale orange juice in its sight window with the level exactly at the third of four unlabelled tick marks (the 0.75 L level).
2. Right recipe jug: level exactly at the third of four unlabelled tick marks too, identical height to the left jug.
3. Each jug's brass scale has exactly 4 (four) evenly spaced unlabelled ticks, the fourth at the shoulder.
4. Urn tap: closed, no drip.
5. Stone front lip: dry, free of utensils.
6. Foreground paving: two separate clear patches of paving beside (not under) the counter support: one at lower-left, one at lower-right, with a gap of paving between them.
Physical inscriptions: none. No numbers, letters or words on any jug, urn or anything else; no tags, no card.
Keep clear and visible: both jug sight windows and levels; the stone lip at lower-right; the two clear paving patches.
Light: amber work lamp, cool moonlight on brass and glass; crisp meniscus lines.
Do not show: different levels in the two jugs; a level at the second or fourth tick; numbers on the scales; tags; a third jug; an open tap; any person, hand or animal; label boxes or arrows.

Use case: ChandRush Chapter 02 location reference plate L05_C, a medium three-quarter view of the dry weighing end of the Food Street drink counter. It establishes the scale, bowl, blank record surface and a transparent mixing jug with a three-quarter target line.
Asset: one 4:3 landscape scenic image of an empty location, no characters.
Input images:
- Image 1: the approved plate L05_A. Use it for: the cream stone slab, indigo panelled timber with brass fittings and star-medallion panels, the brass work lamp and bracket, the paving, the overall finish. Ignore: the recipe card, the recipe jugs, the urn, the reserve bottle and the small brass transfer jug (out of this view or replaced).
- Image 2: the approved Food Street master. Use it only for finish and light. Ignore: all label boxes, annotation words and arrows; the cart, bowls, trolley and table.
Camera and framing: medium three-quarter view from the customer aisle at standing eye height, angled towards the dry weighing end of the drink counter (the Parade end). The cream slab with its pale front edge runs across the lower middle of the frame. An indigo front-panel joint is visible below. The fixed brass lamp bracket is upper-left. The urn and reserve bottle are out of frame.
Place and construction, screen-left to screen-right on the slab:
1. Compact brass-and-cream kitchen scale (left): one flat round weighing platform, a front display window, and one round push button (tare) on its front, beside the display.
2. Clean empty brass bowl just right of the scale.
3. Record surface: a flat blank cream slate lying on the slab front, centre.
4. Mixing jug (right): a separate transparent clear-glass one-litre jug with a handle and pouring lip, quite large in frame (about one fifth of the frame height), with white printed marks on the glass.
5. Small board: a small upright cream board in a brass stand beside the mixing jug.
State at this moment (exact):
1. Scale platform empty. Display reads "0 g".
2. Bowl empty.
3. Record slate completely blank.
4. Mixing jug empty, dry. Near its top a horizontal line marked "1 L". At exactly three-quarters of the height from the base to the 1 L line, a second horizontal target line labelled "¾ OF CAPACITY".
5. Board: an empty rectangular outlined box followed by "%".
6. Slab dry and clear in front of scale, slate and jug.
Physical inscriptions (render exactly, nothing else): scale display "0 g", dark digits on a pale display, about one twelfth of frame width; on the mixing jug glass "1 L" beside the top line and "¾ OF CAPACITY" beside the target line, white printed, legible, fraction with a clean bar; on the board an empty box then "%", large. No other numbers, letters or words: none on the bowl, slate, scale body, panels.
Keep clear and visible: the slab front edge opposite the scale; the tare button; the blank slate; the slab beside the mixing jug; the display, the target line and the empty field.
Light: amber work lamp upper-left, cool moonlight on brass and glass.
Do not show: liquid in the jug; anything on the scale; writing on the slate; a number in the % box; teal recipe jugs or the urn; any person, hand or animal; label boxes or arrows.
